title: The Final Will
premise: True-crime podcaster Casper Okafor has spent seven years documenting the unsolved 1995 disappearance of schoolteacher Maren Voss in the fading town of Hollow Creek, careful never to accuse anyone who might still be listening. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to the crime, the other promising 'the rest of it' if he keeps digging—Casper realizes the confession is a forgery designed to close the case and bury a second, darker truth. Following alibis woven thirty years ago by the town's founding families, he uncovers that Maren was silenced for discovering embezzlement from the town trust, and that his own late father helped forge the cover story. In the end, Casper must choose between publishing the full truth—which will destroy the family of the woman he loves—or letting justice die with the last living conspirator, who is rapidly failing in hospice; he chooses a third path, extracting a recorded deathbed confession and handing it not to the compromised sheriff but to a state prosecutor, trading his podcast's ending for a justice the law can finally own.
about_author: Orsen Vane is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering courtrooms across the American Midwest before turning to fiction. Known for meticulously researched mysteries about secrets that outlive their keepers, Vane writes from a farmhouse where, allegedly, nothing has ever happened.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Seven years into his podcast on Maren Voss's disappearance, Casper gives a tour of his archive—every interview, every contradiction filed away—and reveals why he never names suspects: his father was the town's deputy when she vanished. The beat is controlled obsession masking guilt.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Twin letters arrive: a detailed confession signed by dead handyman Eli Brandt, and an unsigned note reading 'Eli didn't do it. Keep digging.' Handwriting analysis suggests both were written by the same living person. The emotional beat is the thrill of pursuit curdling into paranoia.

chapters.title: The Alibi Season
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Casper and Ruth Calloway, daughter of the town's former bank president. Casper re-interviews the four original alibi witnesses, now elderly, and finds their stories rehearsed to the minute. Ruth's chapters reveal she knows more than she says. Beat: dread beneath polite small-town warmth.

chapters.title: What Maren Kept
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. A storage unit belonging to Maren's sister yields her teaching journals: entries about missing funds from the Hollow Creek Community Trust and a meeting she scheduled the week she disappeared. Someone ransacked the unit before him. Beat: the victim becomes a person, raising the stakes.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Going through his late father's effects, Casper finds a second set of patrol logs for October 1995—pages altered in his father's handwriting. His father wasn't just complicit; he built the timeline everyone still repeats. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Ruth Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: POV: Ruth. Ruth confronts Casper, begging him to stop before the last conspirator—her dying father, Ansel Calloway—is dragged out of hospice. Instead she slips him one fact: the forged confession's paper came from the bank's supply closet. Beat: loyalty cracking under the weight of truth.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. The unsigned letter-writer finally makes contact—a retired court clerk who watched evidence vanish in 1995 and has been testing whether Casper could be trusted. He confirms Maren found the embezzlement and names the man who profited: Ansel Calloway. Beat: the case turns from whodunit to what-now.

chapters.title: The Fire at the Archive
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Arson destroys Casper's studio and most of his archive hours before he planned to air the episode. The sheriff—who owes the Calloways—calls it electrical. Casper realizes the conspiracy isn't historical; it's active, and someone inside it thinks he's nearly done. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Hospice Light
chapters.summary: POV: Casper and Ruth. Casper sneaks into the hospice with a recorder while Ruth keeps watch, torn between protecting her father's name and honoring Maren. Ansel, lucid for the first time in months, confesses to the theft, the silencing, and hiring the forgery—then flatlines mid-sentence. Beat: climax; victory and horror entwined.

chapters.title: The Rest of It
chapters.summary: POV: Casper. Refusing the compromised sheriff, Casper delivers the recording to a state prosecutor and publishes a final episode that ends his podcast—not with the answer, but with the question of what a town owes its dead. Ruth stands beside him publicly. Beat: bittersweet resolution; belonging chosen over safety.
